The present appeal under Section 173 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 has been preferred by the appellant-Insurance Company (for short 'the Insurance Company') against the judgment and award dated 13.01.2017 passed by the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Ajmer (for short 'the Tribunal') in Claim Case No.574/2006 (646/2006), whereby the Tribunal has awarded a sum of Rs.1,18,360/- along with interest @ 6% per annum from the date of filing the claim petition i.e. w.e.f. 05.10.2006 as compensation in favour of the respondent No.1-claimant (for short 'the claimant').
[2024

Learned counsel for the Insurance Company submits that the Tribunal had committed serious error in deciding the issue No.4 against the Insurance Company because vehicle-in-question (tempo) was passenger carrying commercial vehicle and driver was having a license to drive the light motor vehicle only.
So, driver did not possess the valid license to drive the vehicle.
So, judgment and award passed by the Tribunal be set aside.

sentences.text: I have considered the arguments advanced by learned counsel for the Insurance Company and perused the impugned order.

While deciding the issue No.4 against the Insurance Company, the Tribunal rightly held that driver Suresh Kumar who was possessing the valid and effective driving license to drive the LMV, was also authorised to drive the passenger carrying commercial vehicle because unladen weight of tempo was 450 Kg which falls within the category of LMV.

As per judicial pronouncement of Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Mukund Dewangan Vs. Oriental Insurance Company Limited reported in MACD 20174(3) (SC) 74, the driver is authorised to drive carrying commercial vehicle also, the unladen weight of which is upto 7500 Kg.

entities.text: Mukund Dewangan Vs. Oriental Insurance Company Limited reported in MACD 20174(3) (SC) 74
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: So, in my considered opinion, the Tribunal has not committed any error in deciding the issue No.4 against the Insurance Company.
So, present appeal being devoid of merit, is liable to be dismissed, which stands dismissed accordingly.

(NARENDRA SINGH DHADDHA),J Jatin /12 Powered by TCPDF (www.tcpdf.org)
